page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g is a dedicated compute-oriented virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, configured with 24 physical cores across 48 vCPUs and two threads per core. The instance includes 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Architectural features include 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD volume, and no discrete GPU accelerators are bundled.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong raw compute and memory subsystem performance. The server scored 2,607.0 in single-core and 22,510.0 in multi-core Geekbench metrics, landing in the top tier of evaluated systems. Large-block memory throughput reaches 428.71 GB/sec for uncached reads and 201.63 GB/sec for writes. Database execution profiles are highlighted by 33,428.79 points in PassMark database operations and over 91.43 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Supported by AVX-512 vector pipelines, CPU-based LLM inference achieves 432.61 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 69.0 tokens per second for 7B parameter token generation.

The primary tradeoff of the vx1-g-48c-192g is its minimal 1 GB local NVMe disk footprint, which necessitates external block storage or object storage for data-heavy applications. However, its high vCPU count, dedicated core allocation, and large 192.0 GB RAM capacity yield an efficient hardware configuration for distributed computational jobs, software compilation, memory-centric in-memory caching layers, CI/CD pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g is a dedicated x86_64 instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs. It is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, a 1 GB NVMe SSD, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, without integrated GPUs. The instance demonstrates strong computing performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,510.0 and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 428.71 GB/sec. Advanced vector support including AVX-512 VNNI enables capable CPU-driven language model inference alongside strong single-thread operations. Because onboard storage is minimal at 1 GB, persistent data workloads require supplemental storage volumes. The configuration is primarily suited for memory-intensive caching, enterprise software compilation, in-memory databases, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
